articles.title: Jo Marchant: In search of now
articles.summary:
• The concept of 'now' intertwines the realms of physics, philosophy, and psychology, revealing its elusive nature.  
• Our perception of the present moment is shaped by both cognitive processes and the limitations of human consciousness.  
• Time is not merely a linear progression; it is a complex interplay of experiences and awareness that defines our existence.  
• Understanding 'now' challenges us to reconsider our relationship with time and the significance we assign to each fleeting moment.  
• The quest for the present invites a deeper exploration of mindfulness and the essence of being alive in a constantly shifting reality.

articles.title: The self-making world
articles.summary:
• Lamarck's theory of self-making challenges the traditional Darwinian view by suggesting that organisms actively influence their evolution and environment.  
• The resurgence of interest in Lamarckian ideas invites a reevaluation of the relationship between agency and adaptation in the natural world.  
• This philosophical shift emphasizes the interconnectedness of organisms and their surroundings, blurring the lines between nature and nurture.  
• The implications of self-making extend beyond biology, prompting reflections on human agency and the potential for societal transformation.  
• Ultimately, embracing Lamarck's vision could inspire a more dynamic understanding of evolution, where life is seen as a collaborative act of creation.
